PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.01-01: (Problem ID IHST1)--"Turn Two Phones Into a Broadcast Camera" -   Develop a computer-vision system that turns two ordinary smartphones into a broadcast camera. Two phones on a fixed rig at the halfway line each record roughly half the pitch. The system should merge their feeds into a single seamless panoramic view of the full ground, then automatically pan and zoom within that panorama to follow the play, producing a watchable 1080p match video with no camera operator.  (Suggested Components: OpenCV (feature matching, RANSAC homography, multi-band blending), YOLO-class person detector, Kalman or Savitzky–Golay smoothing, ffmpeg, and Python.)
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.01-02: (Problem ID IHST2)--"Automatic Player Identity and Match Statistics" - Develop a computer-vision system that recognises football players automatically and tracks their performance across matches. The system should assign every player a persistent identity with no manual tagging or registration, re-recognise the same player in future matches, and automatically generate per-player statistics — playing time, distance covered, average and top speed, movement heatmap, and approximate possession.  (Suggested Components: YOLOv8, ByteTrack, OSNet or InsightFace, Kalman filtering, Python, and JSON/SQLite output. )
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.02-01: (Problem ID-IHNG1 )  "From AI Generated Code to Running Software" --AI coding tools can now generate a working codebase from a plain language description in minutes. But writing the code is only the first step. Turning that code into something that actually runs still means dealing with dependencies, environment variables, databases, deployment, and the dozen small things that break in between. There is a growing gap between an application being built and an application actually running. Build a system that takes an unfamiliar or AI generated codebase and turns it into a live, working application with minimal human help. It should figure out what the application needs, connect it to the databases and services it depends on, deploy it, watch it run, and recover when something breaks, not just hand back a deployment plan or a list of missing steps. ( A strong solution might: Read an unfamiliar codebase and work out its dependencies and requirements. Configure environment variables, databases and other services automatically. Deploy the application and expose a working, shareable endpoint. Detect a failed deployment, diagnose why, and retry or fix it.)
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.02-02: (Problem ID-IHNG2 ) "Self Maintaining APIs" --Every application depends on other people's APIs, and those APIs never stop changing. Endpoints get renamed, parameters shift, authentication changes, features quietly disappear. Right now, developers usually find out an integration is broken only after it has already failed in production, then spend hours tracing what changed and fixing it by hand. Build a system that watches an API for changes, understands how those changes affect the code or workflows built on top of it, and works out what needs to change to keep things running. It should go beyond differing two specifications, understand how the API   is actually being used, spot what will break, and where possible, generate and test the fix itself.  (A strong solution might: Detect a change between two versions of an API and classify it as breaking or safe. Trace which parts of a codebase or workflow actually depend on the changed behavior. Generate the required fix and test that it actually works. Flag the cases that genuinely need a human to look at.)
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.02-03: (Problem ID-IHNG3 ) "Multiplayer AI" --Most AI interactions are still single player, one person opens a chat, gives an instruction, reads the answer. Most real work is not like that. Launching a product, closing a sale, running support, all of it involves several people working on the same evolving task at the same time, and today's AI tools were not built with that in mind. Build an environment where several people and one or more AI agents can work on the same ongoing task together. People should be able to watch the agent work, redirect it mid-task, hand it a new instruction, assign it a subtask, and see the results, all without the agent losing track of what everyone else has already said or decided. (A strong solution might: Let multiple people join and act on the same live agent session. Keep a shared, persistent memory of the task as it evolves. Let a person interrupt or redirect the agent mid execution without breaking its context. Keep a clear, versioned record of who decided what and when.)
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.02-04: (Problem ID-IHNG4 )"AI Native Compliance Infrastructure" --Compliance work is still spread across spreadsheets, policy PDFs, and someone's memory of what needs renewing. Organizations are supposed to continuously track licenses, deadlines, regulations, and internal policy, but in practice most of that monitoring depends on a person noticing something in time, and people miss things. Build a system that continuously watches an organization's data and activity, catches potential compliance risks before they become problems, pulls together the evidence, decides what should happen next, and keeps a clear record of the whole thing. It should not just answer questions about what a rule says. It should notice a real license expiring, connect that to the transaction it affects, alert the right person, and log exactly what happened and why. ( A strong solution might: Ingest policies alongside real business data, structured or messy. Catch an anomaly and match it to the rule it violates. Judge how serious it is and gather the evidence to back that up. Trigger the right next step and keep an audit trail of the decision.)
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.02-05: (Problem ID-IHNG5)"Proving You're Human" --AI generated voices, faces, and profiles are quietly breaking the old ways of trusting who is on the other side of a screen. A voice is no longer proof. A face is no longer   proof. Platforms increasingly need a way to know a real, unique person is behind an interaction, without demanding their name, ID, or location to prove it. Pick one real scenario, a review platform, a community, a marketplace, an anti bot system, and build a working way to verify a real human is present for that specific case, while keeping identity exposure to a minimum. The output should be closer to a simple, trustworthy signal like verified human than a full identity check, and it should connect cleanly into whatever decision depends on it, approving the signup or releasing the review. (A strong solution might: Use liveness, behavior, or session signals to establish a real person is present. Produce a simple confidence signal without requiring name, ID, or exact location. Resist duplicate or automated attempts for the chosen scenario. Be honest about how confident the result actually is.)
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.02-06: (Problem ID-IHNG6) "Real-Time Scam and Impersonation Defense" --Scams are becoming more sophisticated as attackers combine social engineering with AI generated text, realistic impersonation, and voice cloning. Traditional filters focus on known senders, links, or keywords, while modern scams can look like an ordinary conversation and lean on urgency, impersonation, and emotional pressure instead. Build a system that evaluates a suspicious message, call, or request as it happens and does more than raise a warning. It should judge how likely something is a scam using context, urgency, and impersonation signals, and where the risk is high, take a protective action, notifying a trusted contact, freezing a request, or logging an incident, before real harm is done. ( A strong solution might: Score a message or interaction for scam likelihood using context, not just keywords or known senders. Check a claimed identity against how that person normally communicates. Escalate high risk cases to a trusted contact or human reviewer automatically. Explain its reasoning in plain language so the action taken is never a black box.)
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.02-07: (Problem ID-IHNG7) "The End-to-End Returns Agent" --Buying something online is easy, returning it usually isn't. A customer has to find the order, work out if it's eligible, understand the return policy, arrange shipping, and then track the refund, often across several disconnected pages and emails. The same fragmented process creates real operational load for the business on the other end. Build an agent that takes a plain request like returning something bought recently, and carries the entire return through to completion. It should figure out which order is being referred to, determine eligibility, initiate the return, and keep the customer updated as the refund moves through each stage, without them having to check back manually. ( A strong solution might: Identify the right order from a vague, conversational description. Check return eligibility against a stated policy and explain the result if it's declined. Move the return through its stages, initiated, shipped, refunded, and reflect that state accurately. Notify the customer at the moments that actually matter, not at every step.)
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.02-08: (Problem ID-IHNG8) "Intelligent Employee Onboarding" --When someone joins a company, HR and IT typically coordinate access across email, chat, source control, project tools, documentation, and security systems by hand. Missing one step can delay a new hire's first week or leave a security gap that goes unnoticed for weeks. Build a system that takes basic information about a new hire and works out the onboarding they actually need based on their role and department, then coordinates the setup across the relevant systems. It should reason about what a specific role requires rather than following one fixed checklist for every hire. (A strong solution might: Infer the right onboarding path from a role and department rather than a single static list. Coordinate setup steps across more than one system and track what's actually been completed. Flag a step that failed or needs a human to intervene rather than silently skipping it. Give a clear, real time view of where a given new hire's onboarding stands.)
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.02-09: (Problem ID-IHNG9) "Appointment Lifecycle and No-Show Recovery" --Missed appointments cost healthcare providers and other appointment based businesses real capacity and create extra administrative work. Patients forget, realize they can't make it, or simply don't reschedule, and most systems only go as far as sending a reminder, they don't manage what happens next. Build a system that manages an appointment through its full lifecycle, sending a contextual reminder, understanding the patient's response, handling a reschedule, and where a slot is cancelled, working to recover it rather than letting it sit empty. The interesting part of this problem is what happens after a cancellation, not just before one. ( A strong solution might: Send a reminder and correctly interpret a free text response as confirming, cancelling, or asking to reschedule. Update a calendar and notify the provider automatically when a change happens. Identify who's eligible for a newly cancelled slot and offer it out. Confirm the first person who accepts and close the loop for everyone else.)
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.03-01: (Problem Id-IHCY1)  "ABIAE — Autonomous Brand Intelligence and Anti-Impersonation Engine" - Brand impersonation through cloned logos, fake apps, counterfeit listings and phishing pages is a growing digital-fraud risk. Build an AI-powered system that detects and assesses suspected brand impersonation across selected web, marketplace, app, or social media data. The system should identify suspicious content, distinguish it from legitimate uses such as news or authorised partners, assign an explainable risk score, and automatically generate an evidence report. Teams should also demonstrate basic offender/re-upload linking to identify related cases.  36-Hour MVP: Demonstrate detection on at least one defined data source using organiser- provided, synthetic or publicly available data. Full-scale web crawling and continuous multi- platform monitoring are optional.  Focus Areas: Brand-asset similarity, AI-based detection, intent classification, risk scoring, evidence generation, offender fingerprinting.
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.03-02: (Problem Id-IHCY2) "SentinelEdge — Enterprise Guardrail for Generative-AI Data Leakage" -Build an AI-powered browser security extension that detects and prevents employees from accidentally sharing credentials, source-code secrets, personal data or confidential information with generative-AI platforms or untrusted websites. The system should detect sensitive content locally, intelligently mask or block it, enforce basic security policies, and generate privacy-safe audit events without storing the original sensitive information.  36-Hour MVP: Demonstrate the extension on a supported browser with at least three sensitive- data types, showing detection, masking/blocking and policy enforcement. Centralised enterprise management and cross-browser support are optional.  Focus Areas: Browser extension, local content inspection, secret/PII detection, intelligent masking, policy enforcement, privacy-preserving audit.
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.03-03: (Problem Id-IHCY3) "SynthGuard — Real-Time Deepfake & Voice-Clone Interception"--Build an AI-powered system that detects deepfake or manipulated audio/video used in scams such as fake executive calls, synthetic KYC and fraudulent endorsements. The system should analyse media, identify signs of manipulation, provide an explainable confidence score, and generate an alert with a basic provenance/evidence report.  36-Hour MVP: Demonstrate detection on either audio, video, or both using organiser-provided, synthetic or publicly available test data. Full real-time integration with video calls, social platforms and messaging apps is optional. Focus Areas: Deepfake detection, audio/video analysis, explainable AI
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.03-04: (Problem Id-IHCY4) "IPTrace — Autonomous Patent, Copyright ,Trademark Misuse Detection" --Build an AI-powered system that detects potential misuse of copyrighted content, trademarks, designs or other intellectual-property assets across selected online sources. The system should fingerprint provided IP assets, identify exact or modified copies such as cropped, recoloured or paraphrased content, and distinguish potential infringement from legitimate uses such as authorised resellers or fair use. It should generate a side-by-side evidence report for detected matches.  36-Hour MVP: Demonstrate detection using at least one IP asset type and one defined data source with organiser-provided, synthetic or publicly available data. Global crawling, automated takedown notices and persistent seller tracking are optional.  Focus Areas: IP fingerprinting, modified-copy detection, similarity analysis, legitimate-use classification, evidence generation, repeat-offender tracking.
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.03-05: (Problem Id-IHCY5) "ModelGuard — AI Model-Poisoning , Backdoor Defence" --Build an AI security system that detects data poisoning, backdoors and tampering in the machine-learning model pipeline. The system should validate training data, identify suspicious or poisoned samples, verify model/ weight integrity, and detect abnormal model behaviour or potential backdoor triggers. Findings should include explainable evidence and a basic tamper- evident audit record.  36-Hour MVP: Demonstrate detection of at least one poisoning, backdoor or model-tampering scenario using organiser-provided, synthetic or publicly available data/models. Full end-to-end model supply-chain protection and continuous production monitoring are optional.  Focus Areas: Data validation, poisoning/backdoor detection, model integrity, anomaly detection, behavioural monitoring, explainable security evidence.
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.03-06: (Problem Id-IHCY6 ) "SentinelOps — AI-Powered Security Operations Center (SOC)" --Build an AI-powered SOC assistant that analyses security alerts from multiple sources, reduces duplicate and false-positive alerts, and groups related signals into prioritised security incidents. The system should enrich incidents with relevant context, generate a concise attack narrative, and recommend an appropriate first response for the security analyst.  36-Hour MVP: Demonstrate alert ingestion using organiser-provided, synthetic, or publicly available security logs, with deduplication, correlation, incident prioritisation, and a recommended response. Live integration with multiple enterprise security platforms and automated response execution are optional.  Focus Areas: Multi-source alert ingestion, de-duplication, alert correlation, false-positive reduction, incident prioritisation, attack narrative generation, guided response.
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.03-07: (Problem Id-IHCY7 ) "Ghost Chase — Persistent Offender Fingerprinting Across Reinventions"--Build an AI-powered system that links seemingly different fraudulent websites, apps or accounts to the same potential offender by analysing reusable signals such as code, templates, infrastructure, writing style and behavioural patterns. The system should generate a linked threat-actor profile and explain the signals used to connect related cases, even when visibl identifiers such as domains, logos or account names have changed.  36-Hour MVP: Demonstrate linking of related cases using organiser-provided, synthetic or publicly available data, with at least two types of fingerprinting signals. Large-scale cross- platform tracking and advanced evasion resistance are optional.  Focus Areas: Cross-attribute correlation, code/template fingerprinting, infrastructure analysis, stylometry, behavioural linking, threat-actor graphing.
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.03-08: (Problem Id-IHCY8) "Honeytrail — A Deception Grid of Trackable Decoy Assets" --Build an AI-powered deception system that deploys trackable decoy assets such as fake credentials, documents or honeytoken API keys to detect unauthorised access or suspicious activity. The system should securely trigger an alert when a decoy is accessed or used, capture relevant activity, and provide early-warning insights about the potential attacker and activity pattern.  36-Hour MVP: Demonstrate at least two types of decoy assets in a controlled or simulated environment, with reliable triggering, alerting and basic activity attribution. Large-scale deployment across the web, paste sites or underground channels is optional.  Focus Areas: Honeytoken design, decoy deployment, activity tracking, high-confidence alerting, attacker attribution, proactive threat detection.
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.03-09: (Problem Id-IHCY9) "ScamBaiter — Autonomous Scam-Engagement  & Infrastructure Mapping" --Build a controlled AI agent that safely engages with simulated or authorised scam conversations to identify and extract operational indicators such as phone numbers, payment identifiers, wallet IDs, links and chat handles.The system should structure extracted intelligence, map relationships between identifiers, and generate an actionable report while maintaining strict safety and human-oversight controls.  36-Hour MVP: Demonstrate the agent using organiser-provided, synthetic or authorised scam conversations, with reliable information extraction, basic infrastructure/network mapping and safety guardrails. Live engagement with real scammers is not required.  Focus Areas: Safe conversational AI, identifier extraction, infrastructure
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.03-10: (Problem Id-IHCY10)"Precog — Predicting Malicious Assets Before the First Victim" --Build an AI-powered system that predicts whether newly registered domains, apps or social handles are likely to become malicious before they are used for fraud.The system should analyse early signals such as registration/hosting information, naming patterns, brand similarity and initial behaviour to generate a ranked risk score and pre-emptive warning.  36-Hour MVP: Demonstrate prediction using organiser-provided, synthetic or publicly available data, with a ranked watchlist and explainable risk factors. Real-time monitoring of multiple platforms and large-scale data collection are optional.  Focus Areas: Pre-attack signal modelling, asset analysis, brand similarity, predictive risk scoring, explainability, false-positive control.
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.04-01: (Problem ID -IHAT1) "Intelligent Crop Microclimate Monitoring and Early-Warning System"--Develop a Cyber-Physical System that monitors field-level temperature, humidity, rainfall, wind speed, wind direction, light intensity, and soil conditions. The system should provide localized alerts for heavy rainfall, heat stress, high winds, and unsuitable crop-spraying conditions.(Suggested Components: Ultrasonic Anemometer, Rain Gauge, Environmental Sensor, Soil Spectra, BLE Node, BLE Gateway, and Data Logger.)
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.04-02: (Problem ID -IHAT2) "Predictive Maintenance System for Industrial Machinery used in Farming"--Develop a low-cost machine-health monitoring system that collects vibration and motion data from motors, pumps, fans, and other rotating machinery. The system should identify abnormal vibration patterns, provide a machine-health score, and generate maintenance alerts. PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.04-03: (Problem ID -IHAT3) "Smart Cold-Chain Monitoring and Spoilage-Prevention System " --Design a smart monitoring solution for agricultural produce, dairy products, medicines, or vaccines during storage and transportation. The system should detect temperature and humidity violations, record the duration and location of each violation, and estimate the risk of product spoilage. (Suggested Components: STTS751 Temperature Sensor, SHT-40 Sensor, LIS3DH Motion Sensor, GPS-enabled LTE Data Logger, BLE Node, and Buzzer.)
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.04-04: (Problem ID -IHAT4) "Indoor Air-Quality and Occupancy-Based Ventilation Controller for Controlled Environment Agriculture"--Develop a smart environmental-control system for classrooms, laboratories, workshops, and offices. The system should monitor air quality, temperature, humidity, occupancy, and light conditions and automatically operate a fan or exhaust system when required. (Suggested Components: BME680 Environmental Sensor, Infrared Sensor, Lux Sensor, SHT-40 Sensor, Relay Electrical Switch, BLE Development Kit, and BLE Gateway.)
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.04-05: (Problem ID -IHAT5) "Smart Worker-Safety Wearable" --Develop a wearable CPS prototype for workers operating in factories, construction sites, farms, or other hazardous environments. The wearable should detect falls, sudden impacts, abnormal posture, prolonged inactivity, high temperatures, and excessive UV exposure, and communicate emergency alerts to a supervisor. (Suggested Components: LIS3DH Motion Sensor, UV LTR-390 Sensor, SHT-40 Sensor, BLE Node, BLE Gateway, Flash Memory, and Buzzer.)
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.04-06: (Problem ID -IHAT6) "Offline-Capable Distributed Environmental Monitoring Network" --Develop a resilient sensing network for farms, industrial sites, water bodies, or remote locations with unreliable internet connectivity. The system should collect and store sensor data locally, synchronize missing records when connectivity is restored, and display the connectivity and operational status of each sensing node. (Suggested Components: BLE Nodes, BLE Gateway, ModView nRF52833 BLE + RS485 Data Logger, LTE Data Logger, Memory Board, and Environmental Sensors.)
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.05-01: (Problem Id-IHSA1) "Smart Waste Management" -Waste is not properly segregated and collection is inefficient. (Use AI image classification to identify waste atleast 5 to 6 categories and IoT/data to predict when bins need collection.)
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.05-02: (Problem Id-IHSA2)  " Water Leakage Detection" -Large quantities of water are lost through unnoticed leakage. (Analyze water-consumption patterns using IoT/simulated data and use anomaly detection to identify possible leakage.)
PROBLEM_STATEMENT_NAMES.05-03: (Problem Id-IHSA3) "Campus Energy Optimization" -Electricity is wasted in classrooms and laboratories. (Predict occupancy and energy demand and recommend optimal operation of lights, AC and equipment.)
